title: Noise and last-coordinate restriction
statement: Let $n,m$ be nonnegative integers, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$, let $g$ be an $m$-tuple of such functions, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$. The combined vector formed from the noise-operator images of the restrictions of $f$ and $g$ at $b$, evaluated at $x$, equals the combined vector formed from the noise-operator images of their last-coordinate averages, plus $\sigma(b)$ times the combined vector formed from the noise-operator images of their last-coordinate half-differences.
hypotheses_covered: f is a real-valued function on the (n+1)-dimensional Boolean cube
g is an m-tuple of real-valued functions on that cube
x is a point of the n-dimensional Boolean cube
replaced: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, a real function $h$ on a uniform Boolean cube, and a vector $k$ of real functions on that cube, put $V(h,k)(x)=((D_i h(x))_i,(k_j(x))_j)$ and $F_P(h,k)=\mathbb E\sqrt{P(h)^2+\|V(h,k)\|_2^2}$, where $D_i$ is the coordinate half-difference. Let $f$ be a real function and $g$ a vector of $m$ real functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$. Put $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $g_b(x)=g(x,b)$, $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$, $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, and define $a_g,d_g$ componentwise. Let $T_\rho$ denote Boolean noise with real correlation $\rho$, whose Fourier multiplier on a set of size $k$ is $\rho^k$. For $s_0=1$, $s_1=-1$, $V(T_\rho f_b,T_\rho g_b)(x)=V(T_\rho a_f,T_\rho a_g)(x)+s_bV(T_\rho d_f,T_\rho d_g)(x)$ for every $x,b$.
